/-!
# Conjecture 9.5

by V. A. Gorbunov

A variety of groups is called *primitive* if each of its subquasivarieties is a
variety. Describe all primitive varieties of groups. Is every primitive variety of
groups locally finite?

A *variety* of groups is the class of all groups satisfying some set of laws
(identities) $w = 1$, where $w$ ranges over words in the free group on the countably
many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$. By Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes
of groups closed under subgroups, homomorphic images and arbitrary direct products.
A *quasivariety* of groups is the class of all groups satisfying some set of
quasi-identities
$$u_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_n = 1 \implies w = 1 \qquad (n \geq 0).$$
By Mal'cev's theorem these are exactly the classes of groups closed under subgroups,
direct products (including the empty product, the trivial group) and ultraproducts.
A *subquasivariety* of a variety $\mathfrak{V}$ is a quasivariety contained in
$\mathfrak{V}$. A variety is *locally finite* if every finitely generated group in it
is finite; since a variety is closed under subgroups, this is the same as every group
in it being locally finite.

Classes of groups are modelled as predicates on the groups with carrier in a fixed
universe `Type u`. This loses nothing: membership in a (quasi)variety, inclusions
between (quasi)varieties and local finiteness are all determined by finitely generated,
hence countable, groups, which exist in every universe.

Only the yes/no question is formalised here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` satisfies the law `w = 1`, where `w : FreeGroup ℕ` is a word in the
variables `x₀, x₁, …`, if every substitution `f` of elements of `G` for the variables
sends `w` to `1`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup.lift (used to evaluate the word); Mathlib's ModelTheory `Theory`/`Sentence` machinery has no language of groups and would be far heavier.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.5».SatisfiesLaw
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a group satisfying a law (identity) w = 1 for a word w in the free group on countably many variables; needed to define varieties of groups.

blocks.name: SatisfiesLaw
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` satisfies the law `w = 1`, where `w : FreeGroup ℕ` is a word in the
variables `x₀, x₁, …`, if every substitution `f` of elements of `G` for the variables
sends `w` to `1`. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

blocks.code:
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The words `u` appearing in the premises `u = 1`. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The word `w` of the conclusion `w = 1`. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ
blocks.docstring:
A quasi-identity in the language of groups: finitely many premises `u = 1`
(for `u ∈ premises`) and a conclusion `conclusion = 1`, all words in the variables
`x₀, x₁, …`. A quasi-identity with no premises is a law.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.Sentence / universal Horn sentences in Mathlib.ModelTheory (no group language available; no Horn-fragment notion).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.5».QuasiIdentity
justification.why_needed: A quasi-identity (finitely many premises u = 1 and a conclusion w = 1) has no counterpart in Mathlib; needed to define quasivarieties.

blocks.name: QuasiIdentity
blocks.text:
/-- A quasi-identity in the language of groups: finitely many premises `u = 1`
(for `u ∈ premises`) and a conclusion `conclusion = 1`, all words in the variables
`x₀, x₁, …`. A quasi-identity with no premises is a law. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The words `u` appearing in the premises `u = 1`. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The word `w` of the conclusion `w = 1`. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ

blocks.docstring:
A group `G` satisfies a quasi-identity `q` if for every substitution `f` of elements
of `G` for the variables under which all premises of `q` evaluate to `1`, the conclusion
of `q` evaluates to `1`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.Sentence.Realize (unusable without a Mathlib language of groups).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.5».SatisfiesQuasiIdentity
justification.why_needed: Satisfaction of a quasi-identity by a group; no Mathlib counterpart.

blocks.name: SatisfiesQuasiIdentity
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` satisfies a quasi-identity `q` if for every substitution `f` of elements
of `G` for the variables under which all premises of `q` evaluate to `1`, the conclusion
of `q` evaluates to `1`. -/
def SatisfiesQuasiIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, (∀ u ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f u = 1) →
    FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion = 1

def IsVariety (𝔙 : GroupClass.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ L : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], 𝔙 G ↔ ∀ w ∈ L, SatisfiesLaw G w

blocks.name: IsQuasivariety

/-- A class `𝔎` of groups is a *quasivariety* if it consists exactly of the groups

A variety `𝔙` of groups is *primitive* if each of its subquasivarieties, i.e. each

justification.closest_existing_considered: None exists; built from IsVariety and IsQuasivariety.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.5».IsPrimitive
justification.why_needed: The notebook's problem-specific notion: a variety all of whose subquasivarieties are varieties.

blocks.name: IsPrimitive
blocks.text:
/-- A variety `𝔙` of groups is *primitive* if each of its subquasivarieties, i.e. each
quasivariety of groups contained in `𝔙`, is a variety. -/
def IsPrimitive (𝔙 : GroupClass.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ 𝔎 : GroupClass.{u},
    IsQuasivariety 𝔎 → (∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], 𝔎 G → 𝔙 G) → IsVariety 𝔎

@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsVariety.isQuasivariety {𝔙 : GroupClass.{u}} (h : IsVariety 𝔙) :
    IsQuasivariety 𝔙 := by
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := h
  refine ⟨(fun w ↦ ⟨∅, w⟩) '' L, fun G _ ↦ (hL G).trans ?_⟩
  simp [SatisfiesLaw, SatisfiesQuasiIdentity]

theorem isVariety_subsingleton : IsVariety fun (G : Type u) [Group G] ↦ Subsingleton G := by
  refine ⟨{FreeGroup.of 0}, fun G _ ↦ ?_⟩

theorem isVariety_isMulCommutative :

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question with an implicit universal quantifier over all varieties of groups (equationally defined classes, i.e. closed under subgroups, quotients and direct products): answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ V variety, (every subquasivariety of V — a subclass closed under subgroups, direct products and ultraproducts, containing the trivial group / defined by quasi-identities — is itself a variety) → every finitely generated group in V is finite; care is needed with the universe level of the classes of groups and with the definitions of (quasi)variety, which are not in Mathlib.
claims.reviewer_why: c06's syntactic definitions (variety = class of all groups satisfying a set of laws w=1 over FreeGroup ℕ; quasivariety = class of all groups satisfying a set of finitary quasi-identities; primitive = every quasivariety contained in 𝔙 is a variety; locally finite = every finitely generated member is finite) are the standard Neumann/Mal'cev definitions, need no bespoke ultraproduct construction, keep IsVariety separate from IsPrimitive exactly as the notebook phrases it, and come with proved API/test lemmas. Statement: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ 𝔙 : GroupClass.{u}, IsVariety 𝔙 → IsPrimitive 𝔙 → ∀ G ∈ 𝔙, Group.FG G → Finite G; answer(True) = 'yes', answer(False) = 'no'.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.5

by V. A. Gorbunov

A variety of groups is called *primitive* if each of its subquasivarieties is a
variety. Describe all primitive varieties of groups. Is every primitive variety of
groups locally finite?

(identities) $w = 1$, where $w$ ranges over words in the free group on the countably
many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$. By Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes
of groups closed under subgroups, homomorphic images and arbitrary direct products.

quasi-identities
$$u_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_n = 1 \implies w = 1 \qquad (n \geq 0).$$
By Mal'cev's theorem these are exactly the classes of groups closed under subgroups,
direct products (including the empty product, the trivial group) and ultraproducts.
A *subquasivariety* of a variety $\mathfrak{V}$ is a quasivariety contained in
$\mathfrak{V}$. A variety is *locally finite* if every finitely generated group in it
is finite; since a variety is closed under subgroups, this is the same as every group
in it being locally finite.

Classes of groups are modelled as predicates on the groups with carrier in a fixed
universe `Type u`. This loses nothing: membership in a (quasi)variety, inclusions
between (quasi)varieties and local finiteness are all determined by finitely generated,

Only the yes/no question is formalised here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.5»

universe u

/-- A class of groups, given as a predicate on the groups with carrier in `Type u`. -/
abbrev GroupClass := ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], Prop

/-- A group `G` satisfies the law `w = 1`, where `w : FreeGroup ℕ` is a word in the
variables `x₀, x₁, …`, if every substitution `f` of elements of `G` for the variables
sends `w` to `1`. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- A quasi-identity in the language of groups: finitely many premises `u = 1`
(for `u ∈ premises`) and a conclusion `conclusion = 1`, all words in the variables
`x₀, x₁, …`. A quasi-identity with no premises is a law. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The words `u` appearing in the premises `u = 1`. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The word `w` of the conclusion `w = 1`. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group `G` satisfies a quasi-identity `q` if for every substitution `f` of elements
of `G` for the variables under which all premises of `q` evaluate to `1`, the conclusion
of `q` evaluates to `1`. -/
def SatisfiesQuasiIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, (∀ u ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f u = 1) →
    FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion = 1

/-- A class `𝔙` of groups is a *variety* if it consists exactly of the groups satisfying
some set `L` of laws. -/
def IsVariety (𝔙 : GroupClass.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ L : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], 𝔙 G ↔ ∀ w ∈ L, SatisfiesLaw G w

/-- A class `𝔎` of groups is a *quasivariety* if it consists exactly of the groups
satisfying some set `Q` of quasi-identities. -/
def IsQuasivariety (𝔎 : GroupClass.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ Q : Set QuasiIdentity,
    ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], 𝔎 G ↔ ∀ q ∈ Q, SatisfiesQuasiIdentity G q

/-- A variety `𝔙` of groups is *primitive* if each of its subquasivarieties, i.e. each
quasivariety of groups contained in `𝔙`, is a variety. -/
def IsPrimitive (𝔙 : GroupClass.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ 𝔎 : GroupClass.{u},
    IsQuasivariety 𝔎 → (∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], 𝔎 G → 𝔙 G) → IsVariety 𝔎

/-- Every variety of groups is a quasivariety. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsVariety.isQuasivariety {𝔙 : GroupClass.{u}} (h : IsVariety 𝔙) :
    IsQuasivariety 𝔙 := by
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := h
  refine ⟨(fun w ↦ ⟨∅, w⟩) '' L, fun G _ ↦ (hL G).trans ?_⟩
  simp [SatisfiesLaw, SatisfiesQuasiIdentity]

/-- The class of all groups is a variety (defined by the empty set of laws). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isVariety_all : IsVariety fun (G : Type u) [Group G] ↦ True :=
  ⟨∅, by simp⟩

/-- The class of trivial groups is a variety (defined by the law `x₀ = 1`). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isVariety_subsingleton : IsVariety fun (G : Type u) [Group G] ↦ Subsingleton G := by
  refine ⟨{FreeGroup.of 0}, fun G _ ↦ ?_⟩
  simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, SatisfiesLaw, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of]
  exact ⟨fun _ f ↦ Subsingleton.elim _ _,
    fun h ↦ subsingleton_of_forall_eq 1 fun g ↦ h fun _ ↦ g⟩

/-- The class of abelian groups is a variety (defined by the law `[x₀, x₁] = 1`). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isVariety_isMulCommutative :
    IsVariety fun (G : Type u) [Group G] ↦ IsMulCommutative G := by
  refine ⟨{⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆}, fun G _ ↦ ?_⟩
  simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, SatisfiesLaw, map_commutatorElement,
    FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm]
  exact ⟨fun h f ↦ h.is_comm.comm _ _, fun h ↦ ⟨⟨fun a b ↦ h fun n ↦ if n = 0 then a else b⟩⟩⟩

/--
Is every primitive variety of groups locally finite?

A variety `𝔙` is *primitive* if each quasivariety contained in `𝔙` is a variety, and
it is *locally finite* if every finitely generated group in `𝔙` is finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ 𝔙 : GroupClass.{u}, IsVariety 𝔙 → IsPrimitive 𝔙 →
      ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], 𝔙 G → Group.FG G → Finite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.5»

items: (Quasi)varieties are defined syntactically (classes of groups defined by a set of laws / of finitary quasi-identities) rather than by closure properties (S, H, P / S, P, ultraproducts). These are equivalent by Birkhoff's and Mal'cev's theorems; the syntactic route avoids building group-structured ultraproducts of dependent families, which Mathlib lacks. In particular every quasivariety so defined is isomorphism-closed and contains the trivial groups, and the empty class is not a quasivariety, matching the standard convention.

Laws and quasi-identity atoms are written in the form `w = 1` with `w : FreeGroup ℕ` (countably many variables x₀, x₁, …), rather than `w = v`; in groups `w = v` is equivalent to `w v⁻¹ = 1`, so no generality is lost. Quasi-identities are finitary (a `Finset` of premises), as is standard; the empty premise set makes laws special cases of quasi-identities (proved as the API lemma `IsVariety.isQuasivariety`).

A class of groups is modelled as a predicate `∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], Prop`; the definitions are universe-polymorphic and the theorem instantiates them at `Type` (universe 0), following the repository convention (e.g. Kourovka/1_40). This is mathematically universe-independent: membership in a quasivariety/variety and the locally-finite conclusion are all determined by finitely generated (hence countable) groups, which exist up to isomorphism in every universe.

"Locally finite variety" is formalized as: every finitely generated group in the variety is finite (Neumann's definition). Since a variety is closed under subgroups, this is equivalent to every group in the variety being locally finite. The hypothesis `IsVariety 𝔙` is kept separate from `IsPrimitive 𝔙` (which only quantifies over subquasivarieties), mirroring the notebook's phrasing 'a variety ... is called primitive if ...'.
The Gothic letters 𝔙 and 𝔎 are used as Lean variable names for the classes, matching the notebook's notation for varieties/quasivarieties.
